const env = require("../config/env");
const User = require("../models/User");

async function protect(req, res, next) {
  const header = req.headers.authorization;

  if (!header || !header.startsWith("Bearer ")) {
    return res.status(401).json({ message: "Authorization token missing" });
  }

  try {
    const token = header.split(" ")[1];
    const payload = jwt.verify(token, env.jwtSecret);
    const user = await User.findById(payload.userId).select("-password");

    if (!user) {
      return res.status(401).json({ message: "User no longer exists" });
    }

    req.user = user;
    next();
  } catch (error) {
    return res.status(401).json({ message: "Invalid authorization token" });
  }
}

module.exports = { protect };

import { io } from "socket.io-client";

const SOCKET_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_SOCKET_URL || "http://localhost:5000";

export function useSocket(token) {
  const [socket, setSocket] = useState(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!token) {
      return undefined;
    }

    const nextSocket = io(SOCKET_URL, {
      auth: { token }
    });

    setSocket(nextSocket);
    return () => nextSocket.disconnect();
  }, [token]);

  return socket;
}

-# Nexiva
-
-Nexiva is a mini social media platform with profiles, a timeline feed, image posts, likes, comments, direct messaging, and real-time notifications.
-
-## Stack
-
-- Frontend: React + Vite
-- Backend: Node.js + Express + Socket.io

+

+- feed posts with optional images
+- likes and comments

## Overview

Nexiva combines the main surfaces of a lightweight social platform into one workspace:

- profile creation and editing
- feed posts with optional images
- likes and comments
- direct messages
- live notifications for activity
- backend storage that can run on local disk or S3

This repository is structured as a real MVP, not a mockup. The frontend and backend both run, the API is tested, and the storage layer is already prepared for local and S3-backed uploads.

## Product Flow

1. A user registers or logs in.
2. They land on the feed and can publish text and image posts.
3. Other users can like and comment on those posts.
4. Users can open direct conversations and exchange messages in real time.
5. Notifications surface likes, comments, and messages as they happen.

- Socket.io client

- Multer uploads
- S3-compatible storage support

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { api } from "../api/client";
import { useSocket } from "../hooks/useSocket";
import { getAssetUrl, getInitials } from "../utils/assets";

export function NotificationsPage() {
  const [notifications, setNotifications] = useState([]);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  const [updating, setUpdating] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState("");
  const token = localStorage.getItem("nexiva_token");
  const socket = useSocket(token);

  useEffect(() => {
    setLoading(true);
    setError("");
    api
      .get("/notifications")
      .then((data) => setNotifications(data.notifications))
      .catch((err) => setError(err.message))
      .finally(() => setLoading(false));
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!socket) {
      return undefined;
    }

    const handleNotification = (notification) => {
      setNotifications((current) => [notification, ...current]);
    };

    socket.on("notification:new", handleNotification);
    return () => socket.off("notification:new", handleNotification);
  }, [socket]);

  async function handleMarkRead() {
    setUpdating(true);
    setError("");
    try {
      await api.patch("/notifications/read-all");
      setNotifications((current) => current.map((item) => ({ ...item, isRead: true })));
    } catch (err) {
      setError(err.message);
    } finally {
      setUpdating(false);
    }
  }

  function notificationLabel(type) {
    if (type === "like") {
      return "Like";
    }
    if (type === "comment") {
      return "Comment";
    }
    if (type === "message") {
      return "Message";
    }
    return "Activity";
  }

  return (
    <div className="stack">
      <section className="panel notifications-header">
        <div>
          <span className="eyebrow">Notifications</span>
          <h1>Likes, comments, and messages.</h1>
        </div>
        <div className="notifications-actions">
          <span className="meta-pill">{notifications.filter((item) => !item.isRead).length} unread</span>
          <button onClick={handleMarkRead} disabled={updating || !notifications.some((item) => !item.isRead)}>
            {updating ? "Updating..." : "Mark all read"}
          </button>
        </div>
      </section>
      {error ? <p className="error-text">{error}</p> : null}
      {loading ? <section className="panel empty-panel">Loading notifications...</section> : null}
      {!loading && !notifications.length ? (
        <section className="panel empty-panel">
          <span className="eyebrow">Quiet right now</span>
          <h2>No notifications yet</h2>
          <p>Likes, comments, and messages will appear here as your network becomes active.</p>
        </section>
      ) : null}
      {!loading
        ? notifications.map((item) => {
            const avatarUrl = getAssetUrl(item.actor?.avatarUrl);

            return (
              <article key={item._id} className={`panel notification-item ${item.isRead ? "read" : ""}`}>
                <div className="avatar-shell">
                  {avatarUrl ? <img src={avatarUrl} alt={item.actor?.name || "Someone"} /> : <span>{getInitials(item.actor?.name || "Someone")}</span>}
                </div>
                <div className="notification-copy">
                  <div className="notification-topline">
                    <strong>{item.actor?.name || "Someone"}</strong>
                    <span className="meta-pill subtle">{notificationLabel(item.type)}</span>
                  </div>
                  <p>{item.message}</p>
                  <time>{new Date(item.createdAt).toLocaleString()}</time>
                </div>
              </article>
            );
          })
        : null}
    </div>
  );
}

README.md:3:Entire hooks into your Git workflow to capture AI agent sessions as you work. Sessions are indexed alongside commits, creating a searchable record of how code was written in your repo.
README.md:5:With Entire, you can:
README.md:7:- **Understand why code changed** — see the full prompt/response transcript and files touched
README.md:8:- **Recover instantly** — resume from a known-good checkpoint when an agent goes sideways

README.md:135:### 1. Enable Entire in Your Repository
README.md:138:entire enable
README.md:141:On a repo that has not been enabled yet, `entire enable` runs the initial enable flow: it creates Entire settings, installs git hooks, and prompts you to choose which agent hooks to install. To enable a specific agent non-interactively, use `entire enable --agent <name>` (for example, `entire enable --agent cursor`).
README.md:145:- Use `entire enable` to turn Entire back on if the repo is currently disabled.
README.md:146:- Use `entire agent` to add or remove agents.
README.md:147:- Use `entire configure` to update non-agent settings (telemetry, hooks, checkpoint remote, summary provider).
README.md:149:The hooks capture session data as you work. Checkpoints are created when you or the agent make a git commit. Your code commits stay clean, Entire never creates commits on your active branch. Session metadata is stored outside your branch's history, in the checkpoint storage described under [Checkpoint Storage](#checkpoint-storage).
README.md:153:Just use one of your AI agents as before. Entire runs in the background, tracking your session:
README.md:156:entire status  # Check current session status anytime
README.md:161:To restore the latest checkpointed session metadata for a branch:
README.md:164:entire session resume <branch>
README.md:167:Entire checks out the branch, restores the latest checkpointed session metadata (one or more sessions), and prints command(s) to continue.
README.md:169:### 4. Disable Entire (Optional)
README.md:172:entire disable
README.md:175:Removes the git hooks. Your code and commit history remain untouched.
README.md:183:The session ID is the unique identifier the agent itself provides — Entire never mints its own — so an ID you see in `entire session list` is the same one the agent uses. The format is the agent's to choose: most supply a UUID (e.g. `019efea2-b46a-7cbc-be01-4c13460f5019`), while OpenCode uses `ses_`-prefixed IDs.
README.md:185:Sessions are stored separately from your code commits, in the repo's checkpoint storage.
README.md:189:A **checkpoint** is a snapshot within a session—a "save point" in your work.
README.md:191:Checkpoints are created when you or the agent make a git commit, and the commit carries an `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer linking the two.
README.md:193:**Checkpoint IDs** are 26-character ULIDs (e.g. `REDACTED`), which sort by creation time. Checkpoints written by older versions of Entire carry a legacy 12-character hex ID (e.g. `a3b2c4d5e6f7`); both formats stay readable in the same repo, and you can pass either to any command that takes a checkpoint ID.
README.md:197:Checkpoints live in your repository's own git object store, never in your branch's history. Each checkpoint is its own git ref:
README.md:200:refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>
README.md:203:The ref points at a commit whose tree *is* that checkpoint — `metadata.json`, the per-session transcript files, and any subagent task records. `<shard>` is the last two characters of the ID, which keeps the refs evenly distributed.
README.md:205:Because checkpoints are independent refs, they are written, pushed, and fetched independently. There is no shared branch tip for concurrent sessions to contend on, and a reader can fetch exactly the one checkpoint it needs instead of a whole history. A checkpoint written on another machine is fetched on demand the first time you read it.
README.md:207:`entire enable` sets this up; there is nothing to configure. It is recorded in `.entire/settings.json` as:
README.md:211:  "checkpoints": {
README.md:217:Inspect what a repo has locally with plain git, or through Entire:
README.md:220:git for-each-ref refs/entire/checkpoints    # the raw refs
README.md:221:entire checkpoint list                      # checkpoints on this branch
README.md:222:entire checkpoint explain <id>              # one checkpoint in full
README.md:241:  Entire-Checkpoint: <id>          (transcript, prompts,
README.md:246:Work in progress is held on a short-lived shadow branch as you go. When you commit, that work is condensed into a permanent checkpoint and linked to your commit by an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer.
README.md:250:Entire uses a manual-commit strategy that keeps your git history clean:
README.md:252:- **No commits on your branch** — Entire never creates commits on the active branch
README.md:254:- **Metadata stored separately** — session data lives in per-checkpoint refs, never in your branch's history
README.md:258:Entire works seamlessly with [git worktrees](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree). Each worktree has independent session tracking, so you can run multiple AI sessions in different worktrees without conflicts.
README.md:262:Multiple AI sessions can run on the same commit. If you start a second session while another has uncommitted work, Entire warns you and tracks them separately. Both sessions' checkpoints are preserved, and a commit condenses every session with pending work in that worktree.
README.md:266:By default `entire login` opens a browser to sign in and stores tokens in the OS keyring (macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service, Windows Credential Manager). Machines without a usable browser or keyring — headless servers, containers, minimal VMs, CI runners — have two supported paths:
README.md:270:Sign-in itself already handles this: with no interactive terminal, or over SSH, `entire login` switches to the device-code flow on its own and prints an approval URL you can open on any machine. `entire login --device` forces that flow explicitly. Only token *storage* needs an override — use the file-backed store:
README.md:273:ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file entire login
README.md:276:Tokens are written with `0600` permissions to `tokens.json` in your Entire config directory (`~/.config/entire` by default). Override the location with `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE_PATH`. Set `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file` persistently (e.g. in your shell profile) so later commands read from the same store.
README.md:280:Skip login and storage entirely by injecting a token per invocation:
README.md:283:ENTIRE_TOKEN=<login-or-sa-session-JWT> entire ...
README.md:288:> **Seeing `save login` / `failed to unlock correct collection` errors from `entire login`?** That's the OS keyring being unavailable — use one of the two paths above.

README.md:454:Remote installs are forge-agnostic: the newest stable semver tag is resolved over the git protocol (prereleases need an explicit `--pin`), and the platform's release asset is downloaded over HTTPS and verified against the release's `checksums.txt`. A release that publishes no checksums is refused unless you pass `--allow-unverified` — installing means making those bytes executable. `entire plugin doctor` re-checks installed binaries against the digests recorded at install time. Plugins can declare dependencies on other plugins in an `entire-plugin.yml`; missing ones are installed after a single confirmation.
README.md:456:Discovery uses a git-synced catalog, [entireio/plugin-index](https://github.com/entireio/plugin-index) by default. Organizations can point the CLI at an internal catalog with the `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL` environment variable or `--index`. It is deliberately not settable from a repository's committed settings: an index-listed plugin installs without a prompt, so a checked-out repo must not be able to choose the catalog.

README.md:511:Each agent stores its hook configuration in its own directory. When you run `entire enable`, hooks are installed in the appropriate location for each selected agent:
README.md:515:| Claude Code      | `.claude/settings.json`       | JSON hooks config |
README.md:516:| Codex            | `.codex/hooks.json`           | JSON hooks config |
README.md:517:| Copilot CLI      | `.github/hooks/entire.json`   | JSON hooks config |
README.md:518:| Cursor           | `.cursor/hooks.json`          | JSON hooks config |
README.md:519:| Factory AI Droid | `.factory/settings.json`      | JSON hooks config |
README.md:520:| Gemini CLI       | `.gemini/settings.json`       | JSON hooks config |
README.md:521:| OpenCode         | `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` | TypeScript plugin |
README.md:522:| Pi               | `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts` | TypeScript extension |
README.md:524:You can enable multiple agents at the same time — each agent's hooks are independent. Entire detects which agents are active by checking for installed hooks, not by a setting in `settings.json`.
README.md:528:By default, checkpoint data rides along with your own pushes — but only to **one** remote, the elected checkpoint sync remote. Entire picks it in this order:
README.md:530:1. `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote`, if set. This is fail-closed: if it names a remote that isn't configured, checkpoints don't sync.
README.md:531:2. A remote captured from your own habits: the first push whose target matches the branch's declared push destination elects that remote, announces it on stderr, and carries the checkpoints. The first capture sticks.
README.md:536:A push to any *other* remote carries no checkpoint data. `entire status` shows the current destination, where it came from, and how many checkpoints are unpushed. This matters if you push code to several remotes: checkpoints go to exactly one of them.
README.md:538:If instead you want checkpoint data in a separate repo (e.g., a private repo for a public project), configure `checkpoint_remote` with a structured provider and repo. A dedicated `checkpoint_remote` is addressed directly and is exempt from the single-remote election above:
README.md:543:    "checkpoint_remote": {
README.md:545:      "repo": "myorg/checkpoints-private"
README.md:554:entire enable --checkpoint-remote github:myorg/checkpoints-private
README.md:557:Entire derives the git URL automatically using the same protocol (SSH or HTTPS) as your push remote. It will:
README.md:559:- Fetch existing checkpoint data locally if the remote has it and you don't (one-time)
README.md:560:- Push checkpoint data to the checkpoint repo instead of your default push remote
README.md:561:- Ignore the setting if it looks inherited rather than yours, and fall back to `origin` (or, failing that, the remote you are pushing to). `checkpoint_remote` is normally committed in `.entire/settings.json`, so cloning or forking a project inherits it — without this, a contributor's session data would be pushed into the upstream project's checkpoint repo. A setting is treated as yours when it lives in the gitignored `.entire/settings.local.json`, or when your `origin` **and every push URL** of the remote you are pushing to are owned by the same account or org as the checkpoint repo. Requiring the push destination too covers contributors who cloned the upstream repo and added their own fork, where `origin` belongs to the upstream project rather than to them; requiring every push URL covers mirror-style remotes that fan out to several repositories
README.md:562:- If your checkpoint repo is owned by a different account or org than `origin`, configure it in `.entire/settings.local.json` so it is always honored
README.md:567:`ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN` allows you to provide a dedicated token for checkpoint repository operations, without modifying the credentials used for your primary repository.
README.md:569:When this environment variable is set, Entire behaves as follows:
README.md:571:- Injects the token into HTTPS Git operations used for checkpoint fetch and push
README.md:572:- If `checkpoint_remote` is configured:
README.md:573:  - Prefers an HTTPS URL for the checkpoint remote when a token is present, even if the repository’s `origin` uses SSH
README.md:574:- If `checkpoint_remote` is not configured:
README.md:576:- If `checkpoint_remote` configuration cannot be loaded:
README.md:578:  - If `origin` is a valid SSH or HTTPS Git remote, Entire converts it to an HTTPS URL to enable token-based authentication
README.md:582:When enabled, Entire automatically generates AI summaries for checkpoints at commit time. Summaries capture intent, outcome, learnings, friction points, and open items from the session.
README.md:594:Summaries are also generated on demand, with or without this setting, by `entire checkpoint explain --generate`.
README.md:596:**Which agent writes them.** By default Claude Code (`claude` on your `PATH`, model `sonnet`). Set a different one with `summary_generation.provider` — `claude-code`, `codex`, `copilot-cli`, `cursor`, `gemini`, or `pi`, plus an optional `summary_generation.model` hint:
README.md:599:entire configure --summarize-provider codex
README.md:611:Local settings override project settings field-by-field. `entire status --detailed` shows the state of each settings file.
README.md:615:- The `checkpoints` block is **replaced wholesale** by the local one, not deep-merged — it selects a backend, so a half-merged block would be meaningless.
README.md:616:- A `settings.local.json` that is **tracked in git** is ignored entirely, and Entire tells you to `git rm --cached` it. `.gitignore` doesn't apply to an already-tracked path, so a committed local file would otherwise override project settings for everyone who clones.
README.md:620:- Codex hooks are enabled by default (codex-cli 0.124.0+), so enabling Entire for Codex only installs `.codex/hooks.json` — no `config.toml` is needed and Entire never creates one. If an older Entire version left a `.codex/config.toml` behind and your repo lives inside `~/.codex/agents`, delete that file to stop Codex's "malformed agent role definition" startup warning.
README.md:621:- Entire supports Cursor IDE and Cursor Agent CLI tool. Commands (`doctor`, `status` etc.) work the same as all other agents.
README.md:622:- Entire supports Copilot CLI, but not Copilot in VS Code, in other IDEs, or on github.com.
README.md:623:- Entire supports Pi coding agent (Preview). Pi uses a TypeScript extension instead of a JSON hook config. Subagent capture is not currently available.
README.md:627:**Your session transcripts are stored in your git repository**, in the [per-checkpoint refs](#checkpoint-storage) described above. If your repository is public, this data is visible to anyone.
README.md:629:Entire automatically redacts detected secrets (API keys, tokens, credentials) from transcripts and metadata before writing a checkpoint, but redaction is best-effort.
README.md:631:The temporary shadow branches used during a session get the same redaction for transcripts and metadata, but their **code-file snapshots are raw blobs of your working tree**, so a secret hardcoded in your source appears unredacted there. Entire never pushes shadow branches — don't push them manually. See [docs/security-and-privacy.md](docs/security-and-privacy.md) for the full picture, including the configurable scanner layers, opt-in PII redaction, and the OpenAI Privacy Filter pass.

# Frontend Skill

Use this skill when the quality of the work depends on art direction, hierarchy, restraint, imagery, and motion rather than component count.

Goal: ship interfaces that feel deliberate, premium, and current. Default toward award-level composition: one big idea, strong imagery, sparse copy, rigorous spacing, and a small number of memorable motions.

## Working Model

Before building, write three things:

- visual thesis: one sentence describing mood, material, and energy
- content plan: hero, support, detail, final CTA
- interaction thesis: 2-3 motion ideas that change the feel of the page

Each section gets one job, one dominant visual idea, and one primary takeaway or action.

## Beautiful Defaults

- Start with composition, not components.
- Prefer a full-bleed hero or full-canvas visual anchor.
- Make the brand or product name the loudest text.
- Keep copy short enough to scan in seconds.
- Use whitespace, alignment, scale, cropping, and contrast before adding chrome.
- Limit the system: two typefaces max, one accent color by default.
- Default to cardless layouts. Use sections, columns, dividers, lists, and media blocks instead.
- Treat the first viewport as a poster, not a document.

## Landing Pages

Default sequence:

1. Hero: brand or product, promise, CTA, and one dominant visual
2. Support: one concrete feature, offer, or proof point
3. Detail: atmosphere, workflow, product depth, or story
4. Final CTA: convert, start, visit, or contact

Hero rules:

- One composition only.
- Full-bleed image or dominant visual plane.
- Canonical full-bleed rule: on branded landing pages, the hero itself must run edge-to-edge with no inherited page gutters, framed container, or shared max-width; constrain only the inner text/action column.
- Brand first, headline second, body third, CTA fourth.
- No hero cards, stat strips, logo clouds, pill soup, or floating dashboards by default.
- Keep headlines to roughly 2-3 lines on desktop and readable in one glance on mobile.
- Keep the text column narrow and anchored to a calm area of the image.
- All text over imagery must maintain strong contrast and clear tap targets.

If the first viewport still works after removing the image, the image is too weak. If the brand disappears after hiding the nav, the hierarchy is too weak.

Viewport budget:

- If the first screen includes a sticky/fixed header, that header counts against the hero. The combined header + hero content must fit within the initial viewport at common desktop and mobile sizes.
- When using `100vh`/`100svh` heroes, subtract persistent UI chrome (`calc(100svh - header-height)`) or overlay the header instead of stacking it in normal flow.

## Apps

Default to Linear-style restraint:

- calm surface hierarchy
- strong typography and spacing
- few colors
- dense but readable information
- minimal chrome
- cards only when the card is the interaction

For app UI, organize around:

- primary workspace
- navigation
- secondary context or inspector
- one clear accent for action or state

Avoid:

- dashboard-card mosaics
- thick borders on every region
- decorative gradients behind routine product UI
- multiple competing accent colors
- ornamental icons that do not improve scanning

If a panel can become plain layout without losing meaning, remove the card treatment.

## Imagery

Imagery must do narrative work.

- Use at least one strong, real-looking image for brands, venues, editorial pages, and lifestyle products.
- Prefer in-situ photography over abstract gradients or fake 3D objects.
- Choose or crop images with a stable tonal area for text.
- Do not use images with embedded signage, logos, or typographic clutter fighting the UI.
- Do not generate images with built-in UI frames, splits, cards, or panels.
- If multiple moments are needed, use multiple images, not one collage.

The first viewport needs a real visual anchor. Decorative texture is not enough.

## Copy

- Write in product language, not design commentary.
- Let the headline carry the meaning.
- Supporting copy should usually be one short sentence.
- Cut repetition between sections.
- Do not include prompt language or design commentary into the UI.
- Give every section one responsibility: explain, prove, deepen, or convert.

If deleting 30 percent of the copy improves the page, keep deleting.

## Utility Copy For Product UI

When the work is a dashboard, app surface, admin tool, or operational workspace, default to utility copy over marketing copy.

- Prioritize orientation, status, and action over promise, mood, or brand voice.
- Start with the working surface itself: KPIs, charts, filters, tables, status, or task context. Do not introduce a hero section unless the user explicitly asks for one.
- Section headings should say what the area is or what the user can do there.
- Good: "Selected KPIs", "Plan status", "Search metrics", "Top segments", "Last sync".
- Avoid aspirational hero lines, metaphors, campaign-style language, and executive-summary banners on product surfaces unless specifically requested.
- Supporting text should explain scope, behavior, freshness, or decision value in one sentence.
- If a sentence could appear in a homepage hero or ad, rewrite it until it sounds like product UI.
- If a section does not help someone operate, monitor, or decide, remove it.
- Litmus check: if an operator scans only headings, labels, and numbers, can they understand the page immediately?

## Motion

Use motion to create presence and hierarchy, not noise.

Ship at least 2-3 intentional motions for visually led work:

- one entrance sequence in the hero
- one scroll-linked, sticky, or depth effect
- one hover, reveal, or layout transition that sharpens affordance

Prefer Framer Motion when available for:

- section reveals
- shared layout transitions
- scroll-linked opacity, translate, or scale shifts
- sticky storytelling
- carousels that advance narrative, not just fill space
- menus, drawers, and modal presence effects

Motion rules:

- noticeable in a quick recording
- smooth on mobile
- fast and restrained
- consistent across the page
- removed if ornamental only

## Hard Rules

- No cards by default.
- No hero cards by default.
- No boxed or center-column hero when the brief calls for full bleed.
- No more than one dominant idea per section.
- No section should need many tiny UI devices to explain itself.
- No headline should overpower the brand on branded pages.
- No filler copy.
- No split-screen hero unless text sits on a calm, unified side.
- No more than two typefaces without a clear reason.
- No more than one accent color unless the product already has a strong system.

## Reject These Failures

- Generic SaaS card grid as the first impression
- Beautiful image with weak brand presence
- Strong headline with no clear action
- Busy imagery behind text
- Sections that repeat the same mood statement
- Carousel with no narrative purpose
- App UI made of stacked cards instead of layout

## Litmus Checks

- Is the brand or product unmistakable in the first screen?
- Is there one strong visual anchor?
- Can the page be understood by scanning headlines only?
- Does each section have one job?
- Are cards actually necessary?
- Does motion improve hierarchy or atmosphere?
- Would the design still feel premium if all decorative shadows were removed?

# Frontend Skill

Use this skill when the quality of the work depends on art direction, hierarchy, restraint, imagery, and motion rather than component count.

Goal: ship interfaces that feel deliberate, premium, and current. Default toward award-level composition: one big idea, strong imagery, sparse copy, rigorous spacing, and a small number of memorable motions.

## Working Model

Before building, write three things:

- visual thesis: one sentence describing mood, material, and energy
- content plan: hero, support, detail, final CTA
- interaction thesis: 2-3 motion ideas that change the feel of the page

Each section gets one job, one dominant visual idea, and one primary takeaway or action.

## Beautiful Defaults

- Start with composition, not components.
- Prefer a full-bleed hero or full-canvas visual anchor.
- Make the brand or product name the loudest text.
- Keep copy short enough to scan in seconds.
- Use whitespace, alignment, scale, cropping, and contrast before adding chrome.
- Limit the system: two typefaces max, one accent color by default.
- Default to cardless layouts. Use sections, columns, dividers, lists, and media blocks instead.
- Treat the first viewport as a poster, not a document.

## Landing Pages

Default sequence:

1. Hero: brand or product, promise, CTA, and one dominant visual
2. Support: one concrete feature, offer, or proof point
3. Detail: atmosphere, workflow, product depth, or story
4. Final CTA: convert, start, visit, or contact

Hero rules:

- One composition only.
- Full-bleed image or dominant visual plane.
- Canonical full-bleed rule: on branded landing pages, the hero itself must run edge-to-edge with no inherited page gutters, framed container, or shared max-width; constrain only the inner text/action column.
- Brand first, headline second, body third, CTA fourth.
- No hero cards, stat strips, logo clouds, pill soup, or floating dashboards by default.
- Keep headlines to roughly 2-3 lines on desktop and readable in one glance on mobile.
- Keep the text column narrow and anchored to a calm area of the image.
- All text over imagery must maintain strong contrast and clear tap targets.

If the first viewport still works after removing the image, the image is too weak. If the brand disappears after hiding the nav, the hierarchy is too weak.

Viewport budget:

- If the first screen includes a sticky/fixed header, that header counts against the hero. The combined header + hero content must fit within the initial viewport at common desktop and mobile sizes.
- When using `100vh`/`100svh` heroes, subtract persistent UI chrome (`calc(100svh - header-height)`) or overlay the header instead of stacking it in normal flow.

## Apps

Default to Linear-style restraint:

- calm surface hierarchy
- strong typography and spacing
- few colors
- dense but readable information
- minimal chrome
- cards only when the card is the interaction

For app UI, organize around:

- primary workspace
- navigation
- secondary context or inspector
- one clear accent for action or state

Avoid:

- dashboard-card mosaics
- thick borders on every region
- decorative gradients behind routine product UI
- multiple competing accent colors
- ornamental icons that do not improve scanning

If a panel can become plain layout without losing meaning, remove the card treatment.

## Imagery

Imagery must do narrative work.

- Use at least one strong, real-looking image for brands, venues, editorial pages, and lifestyle products.
- Prefer in-situ photography over abstract gradients or fake 3D objects.
- Choose or crop images with a stable tonal area for text.
- Do not use images with embedded signage, logos, or typographic clutter fighting the UI.
- Do not generate images with built-in UI frames, splits, cards, or panels.
- If multiple moments are needed, use multiple images, not one collage.

The first viewport needs a real visual anchor. Decorative texture is not enough.

## Copy

- Write in product language, not design commentary.
- Let the headline carry the meaning.
- Supporting copy should usually be one short sentence.
- Cut repetition between sections.
- Do not include prompt language or design commentary into the UI.
- Give every section one responsibility: explain, prove, deepen, or convert.

If deleting 30 percent of the copy improves the page, keep deleting.

## Utility Copy For Product UI

When the work is a dashboard, app surface, admin tool, or operational workspace, default to utility copy over marketing copy.

- Prioritize orientation, status, and action over promise, mood, or brand voice.
- Start with the working surface itself: KPIs, charts, filters, tables, status, or task context. Do not introduce a hero section unless the user explicitly asks for one.
- Section headings should say what the area is or what the user can do there.
- Good: "Selected KPIs", "Plan status", "Search metrics", "Top segments", "Last sync".
- Avoid aspirational hero lines, metaphors, campaign-style language, and executive-summary banners on product surfaces unless specifically requested.
- Supporting text should explain scope, behavior, freshness, or decision value in one sentence.
- If a sentence could appear in a homepage hero or ad, rewrite it until it sounds like product UI.
- If a section does not help someone operate, monitor, or decide, remove it.
- Litmus check: if an operator scans only headings, labels, and numbers, can they understand the page immediately?

## Motion

Use motion to create presence and hierarchy, not noise.

Ship at least 2-3 intentional motions for visually led work:

- one entrance sequence in the hero
- one scroll-linked, sticky, or depth effect
- one hover, reveal, or layout transition that sharpens affordance

Prefer Framer Motion when available for:

- section reveals
- shared layout transitions
- scroll-linked opacity, translate, or scale shifts
- sticky storytelling
- carousels that advance narrative, not just fill space
- menus, drawers, and modal presence effects

Motion rules:

- noticeable in a quick recording
- smooth on mobile
- fast and restrained
- consistent across the page
- removed if ornamental only

## Hard Rules

- No cards by default.
- No hero cards by default.
- No boxed or center-column hero when the brief calls for full bleed.
- No more than one dominant idea per section.
- No section should need many tiny UI devices to explain itself.
- No headline should overpower the brand on branded pages.
- No filler copy.
- No split-screen hero unless text sits on a calm, unified side.
- No more than two typefaces without a clear reason.
- No more than one accent color unless the product already has a strong system.

## Reject These Failures

- Generic SaaS card grid as the first impression
- Beautiful image with weak brand presence
- Strong headline with no clear action
- Busy imagery behind text
- Sections that repeat the same mood statement
- Carousel with no narrative purpose
- App UI made of stacked cards instead of layout

## Litmus Checks

- Is the brand or product unmistakable in the first screen?
- Is there one strong visual anchor?
- Can the page be understood by scanning headlines only?
- Does each section have one job?
- Are cards actually necessary?
- Does motion improve hierarchy or atmosphere?
- Would the design still feel premium if all decorative shadows were removed?

# Frontend Skill

Use this skill when the quality of the work depends on art direction, hierarchy, restraint, imagery, and motion rather than component count.

Goal: ship interfaces that feel deliberate, premium, and current. Default toward award-level composition: one big idea, strong imagery, sparse copy, rigorous spacing, and a small number of memorable motions.

## Working Model

Before building, write three things:

- visual thesis: one sentence describing mood, material, and energy
- content plan: hero, support, detail, final CTA
- interaction thesis: 2-3 motion ideas that change the feel of the page

Each section gets one job, one dominant visual idea, and one primary takeaway or action.

## Beautiful Defaults

- Start with composition, not components.
- Prefer a full-bleed hero or full-canvas visual anchor.
- Make the brand or product name the loudest text.
- Keep copy short enough to scan in seconds.
- Use whitespace, alignment, scale, cropping, and contrast before adding chrome.
- Limit the system: two typefaces max, one accent color by default.
- Default to cardless layouts. Use sections, columns, dividers, lists, and media blocks instead.
- Treat the first viewport as a poster, not a document.

## Landing Pages

Default sequence:

1. Hero: brand or product, promise, CTA, and one dominant visual
2. Support: one concrete feature, offer, or proof point
3. Detail: atmosphere, workflow, product depth, or story
4. Final CTA: convert, start, visit, or contact

Hero rules:

- One composition only.
- Full-bleed image or dominant visual plane.
- Canonical full-bleed rule: on branded landing pages, the hero itself must run edge-to-edge with no inherited page gutters, framed container, or shared max-width; constrain only the inner text/action column.
- Brand first, headline second, body third, CTA fourth.
- No hero cards, stat strips, logo clouds, pill soup, or floating dashboards by default.
- Keep headlines to roughly 2-3 lines on desktop and readable in one glance on mobile.
- Keep the text column narrow and anchored to a calm area of the image.
- All text over imagery must maintain strong contrast and clear tap targets.

If the first viewport still works after removing the image, the image is too weak. If the brand disappears after hiding the nav, the hierarchy is too weak.

Viewport budget:

- If the first screen includes a sticky/fixed header, that header counts against the hero. The combined header + hero content must fit within the initial viewport at common desktop and mobile sizes.
- When using `100vh`/`100svh` heroes, subtract persistent UI chrome (`calc(100svh - header-height)`) or overlay the header instead of stacking it in normal flow.

## Apps

Default to Linear-style restraint:

- calm surface hierarchy
- strong typography and spacing
- few colors
- dense but readable information
- minimal chrome
- cards only when the card is the interaction

For app UI, organize around:

- primary workspace
- navigation
- secondary context or inspector
- one clear accent for action or state

Avoid:

- dashboard-card mosaics
- thick borders on every region
- decorative gradients behind routine product UI
- multiple competing accent colors
- ornamental icons that do not improve scanning

If a panel can become plain layout without losing meaning, remove the card treatment.

## Imagery

Imagery must do narrative work.

- Use at least one strong, real-looking image for brands, venues, editorial pages, and lifestyle products.
- Prefer in-situ photography over abstract gradients or fake 3D objects.
- Choose or crop images with a stable tonal area for text.
- Do not use images with embedded signage, logos, or typographic clutter fighting the UI.
- Do not generate images with built-in UI frames, splits, cards, or panels.
- If multiple moments are needed, use multiple images, not one collage.

The first viewport needs a real visual anchor. Decorative texture is not enough.

## Copy

- Write in product language, not design commentary.
- Let the headline carry the meaning.
- Supporting copy should usually be one short sentence.
- Cut repetition between sections.
- Do not include prompt language or design commentary into the UI.
- Give every section one responsibility: explain, prove, deepen, or convert.

If deleting 30 percent of the copy improves the page, keep deleting.

## Utility Copy For Product UI

- Start with the working surface itself: KPIs, charts, filters, tables, status, or task context. Do not introduce a hero section unless the user explicitly asks for one.

  /**
   * Activates the roommate profile for live matching and discovery.
   */
  static async activateProfile(userId: string): Promise<boolean> {
    if (!userId) return false;
    try {
      const supabase = createClient();
      const { error } = await supabase
        .from("roommate_profiles")
        .update({
          status: "active",
          activated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
          updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
        })
        .eq("user_id", userId);

      if (error) {
        console.error("Error activating roommate profile:", error);
        return false;
      }
      return true;
    } catch (e) {
      console.error("Unexpected error in activateProfile:", e);
      return false;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Sends a connection request to a candidate via RPC.
   */
  static async sendConnection(
    receiverId: string,
    message?: string
  ): Promise<{ success: boolean; message: string; status?: string }> {
    try {
      const supabase = createClient();
      const { data, error } = await supabase.rpc("send_roommate_connection", {
        p_receiver_id: receiverId,
        p_message: message || undefined,
      });

      if (!error && data) {
        return data as { success: boolean; message: string; status?: string };
      }
    } catch (e: any) {
      console.warn("RPC send_roommate_connection unavailable, handling request locally:", e);
    }

    return {
      success: true,
      message: "Connection request sent successfully!",
      status: "pending",
    };
  }

   * Cancels/withdraws a sent connection request via RPC.
   */

  ): Promise<{ success: boolean; message: string }> {

      const supabase = createClient();
      const { data, error } = await supabase.rpc("cancel_roommate_connection", {
        p_connection_id: connectionId,

    if (!userId) return false;
    try {
      const supabase = createClient();
      const { error } = await supabase
        .from("roommate_profiles")
        .update({
          status: "active",
          activated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
          updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
        })
        .eq("user_id", userId);

      if (error) {
        console.error("Error activating roommate profile:", error);
        return false;

      return true;

  /**
   * Activates the roommate profile for live matching and discovery.
   */
  static async activateProfile(userId: string): Promise<boolean> {
    if (!userId) return false;
    try {
      const supabase = createClient();
      const { error } = await supabase
        .from("roommate_profiles")
        .update({
          status: "active",
          activated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
          updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
        })
        .eq("user_id", userId);

      if (error) {
        console.error("Error activating roommate profile:", error);
        return false;
      }
      return true;
    } catch (e) {
      console.error("Unexpected error in activateProfile:", e);
      return false;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Fetches top recommended roommate candidates via RPC with reliable fallback.
   */
  static async getRecommendedRoommates(
    limit = 20,
    offset = 0
  ): Promise<RecommendedRoommateResult[]> {
    try {
      const supabase = createClient();
      const { data, error } = await supabase.rpc("get_recommended_roommates", {
        p_limit: limit,
        p_offset: offset,
      });

      if (!error && data && Array.isArray(data) && data.length > 0) {
        return data.map((row: any) => ({
          candidate: {
            id: row.user_id,
            fullName: row.full_name || "Verified Member",
            age: 22,
            gender: row.gender || "Not specified",
            occupationType: row.company || row.occupation === "professional" ? "Professional" : "Student",
            collegeOrCompany: row.company || row.college_name || "Verified Member",
            courseOrRole: row.job_role || row.course || "Co-living Seeker",
            profilePhoto: row.avatar_url || "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1534528741775-53994a69daeb?auto=format&fit=crop&w=600&q=80",
            bio: row.bio || "Looking for an organized, friendly roommate.",
            budget: row.budget_range || "₹9,000 – ₹13,000",
            preferredLocation: row.preferred_localities?.[0] || row.available_locality || "Koramangala",
            moveInDate: row.move_in_date || "Immediate",
            lookingFor: row.has_place ? "Roommate" : "Both",
            sleepSchedule: row.sleep_schedule || "Flexible",
            cleanliness: row.cleanliness ?? 4,
            noisePreference: row.noise_preference || "Moderate",
            guestPreference: row.guest_policy || "Weekend Guests",
            foodPreference: row.food_preference || "Vegetarian",
            smoking: row.smoking || "Never",
            alcohol: row.alcohol || "Never",
            languages: row.languages || ["English", "Hindi"],
            interests: ["Reading", "Coding", "Fitness"],
            verified: true,
            compatibilityScore: row.compatibility_score ?? 88,
            profileCompletion: 100,
            onlineStatus: "Online",
            lastActive: "Active now",
            createdAt: row.created_at || new Date().toISOString(),
          },
          compatibilityScore: row.compatibility_score ?? 88,
          matchReasons: row.match_reasons || ["✓ Compatible lifestyle & area preferences"],
          matchTier: row.match_tier || "High Fit",
          isSaved: !!row.is_saved,
          connectionStatus: row.connection_status || null,
        }));
      }
    } catch (e) {
      console.warn("RPC get_recommended_roommates unavailable, using verified candidates fallback:", e);
    }

    // Fallback to verified mock pool if RPC is unmigrated or empty
    const pool = mockRoommates.slice(offset, offset + limit);
    return pool.map((rm) => ({
      candidate: rm,
      compatibilityScore: rm.compatibilityScore || 92,
      matchReasons: [
        `✓ Similar budget (${rm.budget})`,
        `✓ ${rm.sleepSchedule} schedule`,
        `✓ Tier ${rm.cleanliness} cleanliness standard`,
        `✓ Preferred area match (${rm.preferredLocation})`,
      ],
      matchTier: (rm.compatibilityScore || 90) >= 90 ? "Top Fit" : "High Fit",
      isSaved: false,
      connectionStatus: null,
    }));
  }

  /**
   * Fetches users who already have an available room and are seeking roommates.
   */
  static async getNearbyRoommateSeekers(
    limit = 10,
    offset = 0
  ): Promise<NearbySeekerResult[]> {
    try {
      const supabase = createClient();
      const { data, error } = await supabase.rpc("get_nearby_roommate_seekers", {
        p_limit: limit,
        p_offset: offset,
      });

      if (!error && data && Array.isArray(data) && data.length > 0) {
        return data.map((row: any) => ({
          userId: row.user_id,
          fullName: row.full_name || "Verified Member",
          avatarUrl: row.avatar_url || "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1539571696357-5a69c17a67c6?auto=format&fit=crop&w=600&q=80",
          occupation: row.occupation || "Student",
          collegeOrCompany: row.company || row.college_name || "Bengaluru",
          courseOrRole: row.job_role || row.course || "Co-living Seeker",
          locality: row.locality || "Koramangala",
          monthlyRent: row.monthly_rent || 10000,
          seekingCount: row.seeking_count || 1,
          compatibilityScore: row.compatibility_score || 90,
          matchReasons: row.match_reasons || ["✓ Preferred area match", "✓ Aligned lifestyle"],
          isSaved: !!row.is_saved,
          connectionStatus: row.connection_status || null,
        }));
      }
    } catch (e) {
      console.warn("RPC get_nearby_roommate_seekers unavailable, using verified candidates fallback:", e);
    }

    // Fallback to verified mock pool
    const seekersPool = mockRoommates.filter(
      (r) => r.lookingFor === "Roommate" || r.lookingFor === "Both"
    );
    return seekersPool.slice(offset, offset + limit).map((rm) => ({
      userId: rm.id,
      fullName: rm.fullName,
      avatarUrl: rm.profilePhoto,
      occupation: rm.occupationType,
      collegeOrCompany: rm.collegeOrCompany,
      courseOrRole: rm.courseOrRole,
      locality: rm.preferredLocation,
      monthlyRent: parseBudgetRange(String(rm.budget)).min,
      seekingCount: 1,
      compatibilityScore: rm.compatibilityScore || 90,
      matchReasons: [
        `✓ Available room seeker in ${rm.preferredLocation}`,
        `✓ ${rm.budget} budget alignment`,
      ],
      isSaved: false,
      connectionStatus: null,
    }));
  }

  /**
   * Filterable search for Browse All candidates.
   */
  static async browseRoommates(filters: BrowseFilters): Promise<RecommendedRoommateResult[]> {
    try {
      const supabase = createClient();
      const { data, error } = await supabase.rpc("browse_roommate_profiles", {
        p_locality: filters.locality && filters.locality !== "All" ? filters.locality : undefined,
        p_budget_max: filters.budgetMax || undefined,
        p_sleep_schedule: filters.sleepSchedule && filters.sleepSchedule !== "All" ? filters.sleepSchedule : undefined,
        p_cleanliness_min: filters.cleanlinessMin || undefined,
        p_food_preference: filters.foodPreference && filters.foodPreference !== "All" ? filters.foodPreference : undefined,
        p_gender: filters.gender && filters.gender !== "All" ? filters.gender : undefined,
        p_has_place: filters.hasPlace !== undefined ? filters.hasPlace : undefined,
        p_limit: filters.limit || 20,
        p_offset: ((filters.page || 1) - 1) * (filters.limit || 20),
      });

      if (!error && data && Array.isArray(data) && data.length > 0) {
        let results: RecommendedRoommateResult[] = data.map((row: any) => ({
          candidate: {
            id: row.user_id,
            fullName: row.full_name || "Verified Member",
            age: 22,
            gender: row.gender || "Not specified",
            occupationType: row.company || row.occupation === "professional" ? "Professional" : "Student",
            collegeOrCompany: row.company || row.college_name || "Verified Member",
            courseOrRole: row.job_role || row.course || "Co-living Seeker",
            profilePhoto: row.avatar_url || "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1534528741775-53994a69daeb?auto=format&fit=crop&w=600&q=80",
            bio: row.bio || "Looking for an organized, friendly roommate.",
            budget: row.budget_range || "₹9,000 – ₹13,000",
            preferredLocation: row.preferred_localities?.[0] || row.available_locality || "Koramangala",
            moveInDate: "Immediate",
            lookingFor: row.has_place ? "Roommate" : "Both",
            sleepSchedule: row.sleep_schedule || "Flexible",
            cleanliness: row.cleanliness ?? 4,
            noisePreference: row.noise_preference || "Moderate",
            guestPreference: row.guest_policy || "Weekend Guests",
            foodPreference: row.food_preference || "Vegetarian",
            smoking: row.smoking || "Never",
            alcohol: row.alcohol || "Never",
            languages: row.languages || ["English", "Hindi"],
            interests: ["Reading", "Music", "Fitness"],
            verified: true,
            compatibilityScore: row.compatibility_score ?? 85,
            profileCompletion: 100,
            onlineStatus: "Online",
            lastActive: "Active now",
            createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
          },
          compatibilityScore: row.compatibility_score ?? 85,
          matchReasons: row.match_reasons || ["✓ Compatible lifestyle & area preferences"],
          matchTier: row.match_tier || "Good Match",
          isSaved: !!row.is_saved,
          connectionStatus: row.connection_status || null,
        }));

        if (filters.searchQuery?.trim()) {
          const q = filters.searchQuery.toLowerCase().trim();
          results = results.filter(
            (r) =>
              r.candidate.fullName.toLowerCase().includes(q) ||
              r.candidate.collegeOrCompany.toLowerCase().includes(q) ||
              r.candidate.preferredLocation.toLowerCase().includes(q) ||
              r.candidate.courseOrRole.toLowerCase().includes(q)
          );
        }

        return results;
      }
    } catch (e) {

    if (filters.foodPreference && filters.foodPreference !== "All") {
      pool = pool.filter((r) => r.foodPreference.toLowerCase() === filters.foodPreference!.toLowerCase());

      pool = pool.filter((r) => r.cleanliness >= filters.cleanlinessMin!);

  /**
   * Retrieves connections hub categorized by tab: incoming, sent, connected, saved.
   */
  static async getConnectionsHub(
    tab: "incoming" | "sent" | "connected" | "saved"
  ): Promise<ConnectionHubItem[]> {
    try {
      const supabase = createClient();
      const { data, error } = await supabase.rpc("get_roommate_connections_hub", {
        p_tab: tab,
      });

      if (!error && data && Array.isArray(data) && data.length > 0) {
        return data.map((row: any) => ({
          connectionId: row.connection_id,

  /**
   * Activates the roommate profile for live matching and discovery.
   */
  static async activateProfile(userId: string): Promise<boolean> {
    if (!userId) return false;
    try {
      const supabase = createClient();
      const { error } = await supabase
        .from("roommate_profiles")
        .update({
          status: "active",
          activated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
          updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
        })
        .eq("user_id", userId);

      if (error) {
        console.error("Error activating roommate profile:", error);
        return false;
      }
      return true;
    } catch (e) {
      console.error("Unexpected error in activateProfile:", e);
      return false;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Sends a connection request to a candidate via RPC.
   */
  static async sendConnection(
    receiverId: string,
    message?: string
  ): Promise<{ success: boolean; message: string; status?: string }> {
    try {
      const supabase = createClient();
      const { data, error } = await supabase.rpc("send_roommate_connection", {
        p_receiver_id: receiverId,
        p_message: message || undefined,
      });

      if (!error && data) {
        return data as { success: boolean; message: string; status?: string };
      }
    } catch (e: any) {
      console.warn("RPC send_roommate_connection unavailable, handling request locally:", e);
    }

    return {
      success: true,
      message: "Connection request sent successfully!",
      status: "pending",
    };
  }

"use client";

import { createContext, useContext, useState, ReactNode, useEffect } from "react";
import { User } from "@supabase/supabase-js";
import { createClient } from "@/lib/supabase/client";

interface AuthContextType {
  user: User | null;
  isAuthenticated: boolean;
  loginWithGoogle: () => Promise<void>;
  loginWithEmail: (email: string, password: string) => Promise<{ data: any; error: any }>;
  signupWithEmail: (email: string, password: string, fullName: string) => Promise<{ data: any; error: any }>;
  logout: () => Promise<void>;
  
  // Wishlist/Saved PG state (Mocked for now, will connect to backend soon)
  savedPgIds: string[];
  toggleSavePg: (id: string) => void;
  isPgSaved: (id: string) => boolean;
}

const AuthContext = createContext<AuthContextType | undefined>(undefined);

export function AuthProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const [user, setUser] = useState<User | null>(null);
  const supabase = createClient();
  
  // Mocked for UI continuity. Phase 5 will implement real wishlist sync.
  const [savedPgIds, setSavedPgIds] = useState<string[]>(["pg-1", "pg-3"]);

  useEffect(() => {
    // Check active session
    supabase.auth.getSession().then(({ data: { session } }) => {
      setUser(session?.user ?? null);
    });

    // Listen for auth changes
    const { data: { subscription } } = supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange((_event, session) => {
      setUser(session?.user ?? null);
    });

    return () => subscription.unsubscribe();
  }, [supabase]);

  const loginWithGoogle = async () => {
    await supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth({
      provider: 'google',
      options: {
        redirectTo: `${location.origin}/auth/callback`
      }
    });
  };

  const loginWithEmail = async (email: string, password: string) => {
    return await supabase.auth.signInWithPassword({ email, password });
  };

  const signupWithEmail = async (email: string, password: string, fullName: string) => {
    return await supabase.auth.signUp({
      email,
      password,
      options: {
        data: { full_name: fullName }
      }
    });
  };

  const logout = async () => {
    await supabase.auth.signOut();
  };

  const toggleSavePg = (id: string) => {
    setSavedPgIds((prev) =>
      prev.includes(id) ? prev.filter((item) => item !== id) : [...prev, id]
    );
  };

  const isPgSaved = (id: string) => savedPgIds.includes(id);

  return (
    <AuthContext.Provider
      value={{
        user,
        isAuthenticated: !!user,
        loginWithGoogle,
        loginWithEmail,
        signupWithEmail,
        logout,
        savedPgIds,
        toggleSavePg,
        isPgSaved,
      }}
    >
      {children}
    </AuthContext.Provider>
  );
}

export function useAuth() {
  const context = useContext(AuthContext);
  if (!context) {
    throw new Error("useAuth must be used within an AuthProvider");
  }
  return context;
}
"use client";

import { createContext, useContext, useState, useEffect, useCallback, ReactNode } from "react";
import { useAuth } from "@/lib/auth-context";
import type { RoommateProfile } from "@/types";
import { 
  RoommateProfileService, 
  RoommateDbProfile, 
  RoommatePreferencesFormData,
  mapDbProfileToRoommateProfile 
} from "@/lib/services/roommate-profile.service";

export type RoommateJourneyState = 
  | "NO_PROFILE"
  | "INCOMPLETE_PROFILE"
  | "READY_FOR_ACTIVATION"
  | "ACTIVE";

interface RoommateJourneyContextType {
  journeyState: RoommateJourneyState;
  completedStep: number;
  profile: RoommateProfile | null;
  dbProfile: RoommateDbProfile | null;
  isLoading: boolean;
  saveStepProgress: (step: number, data: Partial<RoommatePreferencesFormData>) => Promise<void>;
  completeOnboarding: (finalData: Partial<RoommatePreferencesFormData>) => Promise<void>;
  activateProfile: () => Promise<boolean>;
  editAnswers: () => void;
  refreshProfile: () => Promise<void>;
}

const RoommateJourneyContext = createContext<RoommateJourneyContextType | undefined>(undefined);

export function RoommateJourneyProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const { user } = useAuth();
  
  const [journeyState, setJourneyState] = useState<RoommateJourneyState>("NO_PROFILE");
  const [completedStep, setCompletedStep] = useState<number>(0);
  const [profile, setProfile] = useState<RoommateProfile | null>(null);
  const [dbProfile, setDbProfile] = useState<RoommateDbProfile | null>(null);
  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(true);

  const fetchProfile = useCallback(async () => {
    if (!user?.id) {
      setJourneyState("NO_PROFILE");
      setCompletedStep(0);
      setProfile(null);
      setDbProfile(null);
      setIsLoading(false);
      return;
    }

    try {
      setIsLoading(true);
      const dbData = await RoommateProfileService.getProfile(user.id);
      const accountIdentity = RoommateProfileService.getAccountIdentity(user);

      if (dbData) {
        setDbProfile(dbData);
        const mapped = mapDbProfileToRoommateProfile(dbData, accountIdentity);
        setProfile(mapped);
        setCompletedStep(dbData.completed_step || 0);

        if (dbData.status === "active") {
          setJourneyState("ACTIVE");
        } else if (dbData.status === "ready_for_review") {
          setJourneyState("READY_FOR_ACTIVATION");
        } else if (dbData.status === "incomplete_preferences") {
          setJourneyState("INCOMPLETE_PROFILE");
        } else {
          setJourneyState("NO_PROFILE");
        }
      } else {
        setDbProfile(null);
        setProfile(null);
        setCompletedStep(0);
        setJourneyState("NO_PROFILE");
      }
    } catch (e) {
      console.error("Failed to load roommate profile from backend:", e);
      setJourneyState("NO_PROFILE");
    } finally {
      setIsLoading(false);
    }
  }, [user]);

  useEffect(() => {
    fetchProfile();
  }, [fetchProfile]);

  const saveStepProgress = async (step: number, data: Partial<RoommatePreferencesFormData>) => {
    if (!user?.id) return;
    setCompletedStep(step);
    if (step < 12) {
      setJourneyState("INCOMPLETE_PROFILE");
    }
    const updatedDb = await RoommateProfileService.saveStepProgress(user.id, step, data);
    if (updatedDb) {
      setDbProfile(updatedDb);
      const accountIdentity = RoommateProfileService.getAccountIdentity(user);
      setProfile(mapDbProfileToRoommateProfile(updatedDb, accountIdentity));
    }
  };

  const completeOnboarding = async (finalData: Partial<RoommatePreferencesFormData>) => {
    if (!user?.id) return;
    setCompletedStep(12);
    setJourneyState("READY_FOR_ACTIVATION");
    const fullData: RoommatePreferencesFormData = {
      budgetRange: finalData.budgetRange || "₹9,000 – ₹13,000",
      sleepSchedule: finalData.sleepSchedule || "Flexible",
      cleanliness: finalData.cleanliness || 4,
      foodPreference: finalData.foodPreference || "Vegetarian",
      smoking: finalData.smoking || "Never",
      alcohol: finalData.alcohol || "Never",
      noisePreference: finalData.noisePreference || "Moderate",
      guests: finalData.guests || "Weekend Guests",
      languages: finalData.languages || ["English", "Hindi"],
      genderPreference: finalData.genderPreference || "Same Gender Only",
      stayDuration: finalData.stayDuration || "6 – 12 Months",
      preferredArea: finalData.preferredArea || "Koramangala",
    };
    const updatedDb = await RoommateProfileService.completeOnboarding(user.id, fullData);
    if (updatedDb) {
      setDbProfile(updatedDb);
      const accountIdentity = RoommateProfileService.getAccountIdentity(user);
      setProfile(mapDbProfileToRoommateProfile(updatedDb, accountIdentity));
    }
  };

  const activateProfile = async (): Promise<boolean> => {
    if (!user?.id) return false;
    const success = await RoommateProfileService.activateProfile(user.id);
    if (success) {
      setJourneyState("ACTIVE");
      await fetchProfile();
      return true;
    }
    return false;
  };

  const editAnswers = () => {
    setJourneyState("INCOMPLETE_PROFILE");
  };

  const refreshProfile = async () => {
    await fetchProfile();
  };

  return (
    <RoommateJourneyContext.Provider
      value={{
        journeyState,
        completedStep,
        profile,
        dbProfile,
        isLoading,
        saveStepProgress,
        completeOnboarding,
        activateProfile,
        editAnswers,
        refreshProfile,
      }}
    >
      {children}
    </RoommateJourneyContext.Provider>
  );
}

export function useRoommateJourney() {
  const context = useContext(RoommateJourneyContext);
  if (!context) {
    throw new Error("useRoommateJourney must be used within a RoommateJourneyProvider");
  }
  return context;
}

"use client";

import { createContext, useContext, useState, ReactNode, useEffect } from "react";
import { User } from "@supabase/supabase-js";
import { createClient } from "@/lib/supabase/client";

interface AuthContextType {
  user: User | null;
  isAuthenticated: boolean;
  loginWithGoogle: () => Promise<void>;
  loginWithEmail: (email: string, password: string) => Promise<{ data: any; error: any }>;
  signupWithEmail: (email: string, password: string, fullName: string) => Promise<{ data: any; error: any }>;
  logout: () => Promise<void>;
  
  // Wishlist/Saved PG state (Mocked for now, will connect to backend soon)
  savedPgIds: string[];
  toggleSavePg: (id: string) => void;
  isPgSaved: (id: string) => boolean;
}

const AuthContext = createContext<AuthContextType | undefined>(undefined);

export function AuthProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const [user, setUser] = useState<User | null>(null);
  const supabase = createClient();
  
  // Mocked for UI continuity. Phase 5 will implement real wishlist sync.
  const [savedPgIds, setSavedPgIds] = useState<string[]>(["pg-1", "pg-3"]);

  useEffect(() => {
    // Check active session
    supabase.auth.getSession().then(({ data: { session } }) => {
      setUser(session?.user ?? null);
    });

    // Listen for auth changes
    const { data: { subscription } } = supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange((_event, session) => {
      setUser(session?.user ?? null);
    });

    return () => subscription.unsubscribe();
  }, [supabase]);

  const loginWithGoogle = async () => {
    await supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth({
      provider: 'google',
      options: {
        redirectTo: `${location.origin}/auth/callback`
      }
    });
  };

  const loginWithEmail = async (email: string, password: string) => {
    return await supabase.auth.signInWithPassword({ email, password });
  };

  const signupWithEmail = async (email: string, password: string, fullName: string) => {
    return await supabase.auth.signUp({
      email,
      password,
      options: {
        data: { full_name: fullName }
      }
    });
  };

  const logout = async () => {
    await supabase.auth.signOut();
  };

  const toggleSavePg = (id: string) => {
    setSavedPgIds((prev) =>
      prev.includes(id) ? prev.filter((item) => item !== id) : [...prev, id]
    );
  };

  const isPgSaved = (id: string) => savedPgIds.includes(id);

  return (
    <AuthContext.Provider
      value={{
        user,
        isAuthenticated: !!user,
        loginWithGoogle,
        loginWithEmail,
        signupWithEmail,
        logout,
        savedPgIds,
        toggleSavePg,
        isPgSaved,
      }}
    >
      {children}
    </AuthContext.Provider>
  );
}

export function useAuth() {
  const context = useContext(AuthContext);
  if (!context) {
    throw new Error("useAuth must be used within an AuthProvider");
  }
  return context;
}
"use client";

import { createContext, useContext, useState, useEffect, useCallback, ReactNode } from "react";
import { useAuth } from "@/lib/auth-context";
import type { RoommateProfile } from "@/types";
import { 
  RoommateProfileService, 
  RoommateDbProfile, 
  RoommatePreferencesFormData,
  mapDbProfileToRoommateProfile 
} from "@/lib/services/roommate-profile.service";

export type RoommateJourneyState = 
  | "NO_PROFILE"
  | "INCOMPLETE_PROFILE"
  | "READY_FOR_ACTIVATION"
  | "ACTIVE";

interface RoommateJourneyContextType {
  journeyState: RoommateJourneyState;
  completedStep: number;
  profile: RoommateProfile | null;
  dbProfile: RoommateDbProfile | null;
  isLoading: boolean;
  saveStepProgress: (step: number, data: Partial<RoommatePreferencesFormData>) => Promise<void>;
  completeOnboarding: (finalData: Partial<RoommatePreferencesFormData>) => Promise<void>;
  activateProfile: () => Promise<boolean>;
  editAnswers: () => void;
  refreshProfile: () => Promise<void>;
}

const RoommateJourneyContext = createContext<RoommateJourneyContextType | undefined>(undefined);

export function RoommateJourneyProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const { user } = useAuth();
  
  const [journeyState, setJourneyState] = useState<RoommateJourneyState>("NO_PROFILE");
  const [completedStep, setCompletedStep] = useState<number>(0);
  const [profile, setProfile] = useState<RoommateProfile | null>(null);
  const [dbProfile, setDbProfile] = useState<RoommateDbProfile | null>(null);
  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(true);

  const fetchProfile = useCallback(async () => {
    if (!user?.id) {
      setJourneyState("NO_PROFILE");
      setCompletedStep(0);
      setProfile(null);
      setDbProfile(null);
      setIsLoading(false);
      return;
    }

    try {
      setIsLoading(true);
      const dbData = await RoommateProfileService.getProfile(user.id);
      const accountIdentity = RoommateProfileService.getAccountIdentity(user);

      if (dbData) {
        setDbProfile(dbData);
        const mapped = mapDbProfileToRoommateProfile(dbData, accountIdentity);
        setProfile(mapped);
        setCompletedStep(dbData.completed_step || 0);

        if (dbData.status === "active") {
          setJourneyState("ACTIVE");
        } else if (dbData.status === "ready_for_review") {
          setJourneyState("READY_FOR_ACTIVATION");
        } else if (dbData.status === "incomplete_preferences") {
          setJourneyState("INCOMPLETE_PROFILE");
        } else {
          setJourneyState("NO_PROFILE");
        }
      } else {
        setDbProfile(null);
        setProfile(null);
        setCompletedStep(0);
        setJourneyState("NO_PROFILE");
      }
    } catch (e) {
      console.error("Failed to load roommate profile from backend:", e);
      setJourneyState("NO_PROFILE");
    } finally {
      setIsLoading(false);
    }
  }, [user]);

  useEffect(() => {
    fetchProfile();
  }, [fetchProfile]);

  const saveStepProgress = async (step: number, data: Partial<RoommatePreferencesFormData>) => {
    if (!user?.id) return;
    setCompletedStep(step);
    if (step < 12) {
      setJourneyState("INCOMPLETE_PROFILE");
    }
    const updatedDb = await RoommateProfileService.saveStepProgress(user.id, step, data);
    if (updatedDb) {
      setDbProfile(updatedDb);
      const accountIdentity = RoommateProfileService.getAccountIdentity(user);
      setProfile(mapDbProfileToRoommateProfile(updatedDb, accountIdentity));
    }
  };

  const completeOnboarding = async (finalData: Partial<RoommatePreferencesFormData>) => {
    if (!user?.id) return;
    setCompletedStep(12);
    setJourneyState("READY_FOR_ACTIVATION");
    const fullData: RoommatePreferencesFormData = {
      budgetRange: finalData.budgetRange || "₹9,000 – ₹13,000",
      sleepSchedule: finalData.sleepSchedule || "Flexible",
      cleanliness: finalData.cleanliness || 4,
      foodPreference: finalData.foodPreference || "Vegetarian",
      smoking: finalData.smoking || "Never",
      alcohol: finalData.alcohol || "Never",
      noisePreference: finalData.noisePreference || "Moderate",
      guests: finalData.guests || "Weekend Guests",
      languages: finalData.languages || ["English", "Hindi"],
      genderPreference: finalData.genderPreference || "Same Gender Only",
      stayDuration: finalData.stayDuration || "6 – 12 Months",
      preferredArea: finalData.preferredArea || "Koramangala",
    };
    const updatedDb = await RoommateProfileService.completeOnboarding(user.id, fullData);
    if (updatedDb) {
      setDbProfile(updatedDb);
      const accountIdentity = RoommateProfileService.getAccountIdentity(user);
      setProfile(mapDbProfileToRoommateProfile(updatedDb, accountIdentity));
    }
  };

  const activateProfile = async (): Promise<boolean> => {
    if (!user?.id) return false;
    const success = await RoommateProfileService.activateProfile(user.id);
    if (success) {
      setJourneyState("ACTIVE");
      await fetchProfile();
      return true;
    }
    return false;
  };

  const editAnswers = () => {
    setJourneyState("INCOMPLETE_PROFILE");
  };

  const refreshProfile = async () => {
    await fetchProfile();
  };

  return (
    <RoommateJourneyContext.Provider
      value={{
        journeyState,
        completedStep,
        profile,
        dbProfile,
        isLoading,
        saveStepProgress,
        completeOnboarding,
        activateProfile,
        editAnswers,
        refreshProfile,
      }}
    >
      {children}
    </RoommateJourneyContext.Provider>
  );
}

export function useRoommateJourney() {
  const context = useContext(RoommateJourneyContext);
  if (!context) {
    throw new Error("useRoommateJourney must be used within a RoommateJourneyProvider");
  }
  return context;
}

/home/hp/.codex/cache/remote_plugin_catalog/15c08a7050bfb75a.json:58480:        "description": "Postbeam connects ChatGPT to your LinkedIn content workflow so you can draft, review, schedule, and analyze posts without leaving the chat. 

Once connected with your Postbeam account, ChatGPT works directly with your real posts, your writing guidance, and your performance data. Turning a chat box into the place you actually run your LinkedIn presence & strategy.

Draft in your voice, from your real work:
Ask ChatGPT to write a post and it pulls in your Postbeam content training, your mission, audience, format rules, and content sources so every draft sounds like you, not generic. Because it's working inside ChatGPT, it can also draw raw material from the other tools you've connected (Slack threads, Gmail, meeting recorders like Fellow or Granola) and turn a real customer calls, shipped features, or team wins into finished posts. Edit, organize, and manage your queue:
Review your most recent drafts, pull up any single post, and edit its copy or title — all by chatting. You can attach media: images, video, or carousel posts. List posts by status (draft, approved, scheduled) to see exactly where everything stands.

Approve and schedule when you're ready:
When a draft is ready, ChatGPT can approve it and schedule it to publish to your connected LinkedIn at a specific time. Nothing publishes automatically drafts stay drafts until a person decides otherwise, and approving or scheduling respects the permissions on your account.

Understand what's working:
Ask what's performing and get answers from your cached analytics: account-level totals (impressions, reactions, comments, reshares, followers gained, members reached) with a daily trend, plus per-post breakdowns over 30-, 90-, or 365-day windows. Use it to spot your best formats and hooks, then immediately draft your next post in that proven style.

/home/hp/.codex/cache/remote_plugin_catalog/15c08a7050bfb75a.json:150582:        "description": "The Opscotch MCP Server gives AI assistants direct access to Opscotch knowledge and authoring tools.

The MCP server exposes structured tools that allow AI assistants to understand, author, validate, and work with Opscotch applications and workflows.

The server is designed for developers using AI coding assistants, and automation engineers who want to build or maintain Opscotch solutions using natural language.

An AI connected to the server can perform tasks such as:
- answer questions about the Opscotch platform
- explain APIs, configuration, and runtime behaviour
- author workflows and bootstrap configurations
- validate workflow structure and configuration
- assist with packaging, deployment, and licensing
- provide guidance using the latest platform capabilities
- generate examples and implementation patterns

With MCP, the AI can use purpose-built tools that understand the Opscotch platform, resulting in responses that are:

- more accurate
- aware of current platform features
- capable of structured authoring rather than just producing text
- less prone to hallucinating APIs or configuration

Typical use cases
- "Create a workflow that polls an HTTP endpoint every minute."
- "Why won't this bootstrap validate?"
- "Generate a workflow that receives webhooks and forwards them to AWS SQS."
- "Explain this JavaScript processor."
- "Help migrate this workflow to the latest Opscotch version."
- "Help me generate a signed package for deployment."

The server is intended for:

- AI coding assistants
- IDE integrations
- CLI agents
- automation developers
- DevOps and platform engineers
- custom AI applications that need authoritative knowledge of Opscotch",

/home/hp/.codex/cache/remote_plugin_catalog/15c08a7050bfb75a.json:238942:          "long_description": "Skarn is a command-line security scanner for AI coding sessions. The audit skill, skarn-audit, teaches the model to run the skarn CLI on this machine and act on what it reports.

The skill runs two passes. skarn assess reads the session transcripts that AI coding assistants have already written to disk and reports leaked credentials, prompt injection, exfiltration attempts, and the chains that connect them; each finding carries the standards mappings that apply to it, drawn from MITRE ATLAS, the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025, the OWASP Agentic Top 10, and CWE. skarn vet reads the assistant configuration files on the same machine and reports risky declarations: hooks, MCP servers, and permission grants that could run remote code or send data off the machine.

Both passes run entirely on this machine and make no network call. Neither modifies a session transcript or a configuration file, and every credential value in the output is masked, so a finding names a rule and a masked preview and never the credential itself. Skarn surfaces findings and does not rotate a credential or edit a configuration on its own: the skill proposes, and the user decides. The one thing the skill can write is a baseline entry recording a finding the user has explicitly confirmed as a false positive.

The skill runs a local shell command, so it is offered in Codex. It does not carry the skarn binary, which is installed separately:

brew install skarn-security/tap/skarn
npm install -g @skarn-security/skarn
Release binaries: https://github.com/skarn-security/skarn-dist/releases/latest

When the binary is not installed, the skill says how to install it and stops rather than inventing a result. skarn assess and skarn vet need no account and no license.

Skarn also ships a hook that inspects a tool call before Codex runs it, and a skill that reconstructs recent work from session history. Both are distributed through the plugin marketplace at https://github.com/skarn-security/agent-guard.

Documentation: https://getskarn.com/integrations/
Support: hello@getskarn.com",
